newsitem.title: USA: Clinton budget assumes 0.3 point reduction in CPI.
newsitem.headline: Clinton budget assumes 0.3 point reduction in CPI.

text.p: President Clinton's budget proposal for fiscal year 1998 assumes a 0.3 percentage point annual reduction in the Consumer Price Index during 1997-1998.
The reduction would stem from technical improvements made by the Labor Department's Bureau of Labor Statistics.
The White House projects a rise of 2.6 percent in the index in 1997 and increases of 2.7 percent for each of the subsequent years through 2002.

"The CPI would continue to grow about 3.0 percent during 1997-1998 if not for methodological improvements already instituted or planned by the Bureau of Labor Statistics," the budget plan said. "These are expected to trim the annual growth by about 0.3 percentage point."
